output.proposal: HB No. 11067, the proposed S.A.F.E. (Secure and Firearm-Free Education) Schools Act, seeks to establish a comprehensive school safety and weapon prevention program under which the DepEd, school administrations, LGUs and barangays jointly implement measures to prevent the entry of weapons into schools. It aims to ensure that educational institutions are safe, secure and conducive to learning while protecting the rights of learners.
output.alignment: Although catalogued as a government organization and mandates measure, the bill creates no new agency; it assigns new mandates to the DepEd, LGUs and barangays and requires Behavioral Threat Assessment Teams in all school divisions and School Safety Committees in every school. The review should therefore examine whether these new teams and committees duplicate existing school-level and local child protection structures, such as the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children, consistent with the intent of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231) to reduce overlapping functions. The measure aligns primarily with the Human Capital Development priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework, given its focus on safe learning environments as a condition for equitable access to quality education, and secondarily with the Implementation of Full Devolution to LGUs priority area, given the role assigned to LGUs and barangays and the proposed use of the Special Education Fund. The bill is not among the measures in the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11067 seeks to establish a comprehensive school safety and weapon prevention program, to be known as the S.A.F.E. (Secure and Firearm-Free Education) Schools Act, implemented jointly by the DepEd, school administrations, LGUs and barangays. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 2 (Declaration of Policy) provides that school safety requires a whole-of-community approach and that security measures shall be child-sensitive, non-discriminatory, proportionate and respectful of learners' rights.
b. Section 3 (Definition of Terms) defines weapons, school zones covering a 50-meter radius from the school boundary or principal entrances, Crime Prevention through Environmental Design, Behavioral Threat Assessment and the Anonymous Digital Tip Line.
c. Section 4 (Mandates of the Department of Education (DepEd)) provides that the DepEd shall be the lead agency and shall formulate a National School Access Control Policy, establish a national framework for an Anonymous Digital Tip Line, mandate Behavioral Threat Assessment Teams in all school divisions, and set minimum standards for a School Safety Committee in every school.
d. Section 5 (Responsibilities of School Administrations) provides that all public and private basic education institutions shall implement access control with a single point of entry, reasonable bag inspections, parental involvement agreements, and the confiscation and reporting of weapons to the PNP.
e. Section 6 (Role of Local Government Units (LGUs)) provides that city and municipal LGUs shall allocate a portion of the Special Education Fund for security infrastructure such as perimeter hardening, access-control systems and AI-enhanced CCTV, enact local ordinances on weapons in school zones, and coordinate with the PNP on patrols.
f. Section 7 (Duties of the Barangay) provides that barangays shall deploy tanods for perimeter patrols, use the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children for early intervention, and establish a community watch system.
g. Section 8 (Interventions for Minors) provides that students found with weapons shall not be placed in adult penal facilities and that the LSWDO shall provide assessment and intervention consistent with RA No. 9344.
h. Section 9 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the DepEd's current year appropriations, with continued funding included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
i. Section 10 (Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR)) provides that the DepEd, in consultation with the DILG, the PNP and the DSWD, shall issue the IRR within 60 days, prescribing minimum safety standards, and shall submit an annual report to Congress.
output.related_measures_policy: No related bill in the current or past Congresses is identified for HB No. 11067. The measure may be considered alongside RA No. 9344 (Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006), which governs the interventions under Section 8 (Interventions for Minors), and RA No. 7610, whose protections are preserved under Section 12 (Repealing Clause). The measure aligns with the Human Capital Development priority of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework and relates to the Implementation of Full Devolution to LGUs priority. The review should assess whether the Behavioral Threat Assessment Teams and School Safety Committees under Section 4 (Mandates of the Department of Education (DepEd)) overlap with existing child protection and local bodies, consistent with the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231), and whether the use of the Special Education Fund under Section 6 (Role of Local Government Units (LGUs)) is feasible for LGUs with limited fiscal capacity.
